items.title: August Laurent Interview, 1960-03-21
items.q: I was wondering some more about your lessons with Papa Teo. What did he teach you? ... Papa Teo was very good. He taught, he taught you all kinds of... He'd teach you the cards that you could pick up easily.

ctx.x: What part of town were you born in? Were you born right here in the city of New Orleans?

In the 7th Ward. That's why I moved back down here. I'm born right there. Prairie and La Perouse. You heard Big Iloy? Oh yes you heard man. I was living in the middle of the block. Big Iloy was living at that corner. Pico was living around the corner. Lorenzo Teo was living two blocks from me. Papa Teo was living a block and a half this way from me. I was right in them.

I don't like to bother you with all those details but if we can figure out where some of those fellas lived. Like Big I. Now what corner was that on about? Which street? Like Big Iloy. Just which street?

items.title: August Laurent Interview, 1960-03-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I was wondering about Lorenzo's father, the old man Tio... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, that was his uncle.

ctx.x: It ain't the same. Well, your fingers done got all stiff and out of whack. Your lips done got bad. Your wind done got bad. You forget, you forget the breathing space that you would take on certain measures and passages. You see, you can take breathing space on certain passages and measures and just continue on through. Well, if you don't catch the right breathing space, you'll never make that passage all in one slur.
I was wondering about Lorenzo's father, the old man Tio, and the Papa Tio. Papa Tio was his uncle. Uncle.
